cards.title: A mutual fund is a shared basket
cards.body: Lakhs of people pool their money. A professional manager buys many stocks or bonds with it. You own a slice of the whole basket, not one company.

cards.title: The price of a slice is its [[nav|NAV]]
cards.body: If NAV is ₹50 and you invest ₹100, you get 2 units. A higher NAV doesn't mean "expensive". It's just the price of one slice.

cards.title: A [[sip|SIP]] is investing on autopilot
cards.body: Pick an amount, like ₹100, and a date. It gets invested every month. No timing the market, no daily decisions.

cards.title: Why SIPs suit beginners
cards.body: When prices fall, your ₹100 buys more units. When they rise, fewer. Over time this averages out your cost. It's called rupee cost averaging.

cards.question: NAV is ₹25 and your SIP is ₹100. How many units do you get?
cards.explanation: ₹100 ÷ ₹25 = 4 units. Next month's NAV decides next month's units. When the NAV drops, the same ₹100 buys you more.
